title: Torsors under finite locally constant sheaves
statement:
Let $\mathcal G$ be a finite locally constant sheaf of groups on $\et X$
and let $P$ be a $\mathcal G$-torsor. Then $P$ is trivial on an étale
cover of $X$.

external.place: A $G_X$-torsor is representable by a scheme $P\to X$ finite étale (locally on $X$ it is $\bigsqcup_{g\in G}X$, and the transition functions are locally constant permutations; see SGA 4); since $P\to X$ is étale and surjective it is an étale cover, and $P$ restricted to $P$ has the tautological section, so it is trivial there.

proof.text:
Working on the members of a trivialising cover of $\mathcal G$ we may
assume $\mathcal G=G_X$ for a finite group $G$. A $G_X$-torsor is
representable by a scheme $P\to X$ finite étale (locally on $X$ it is
$\bigsqcup_{g\in G}X$, and the transition functions are locally constant
permutations; see SGA 4); since $P\to X$ is étale and
surjective it is an étale cover, and $P$ restricted to $P$ has the
tautological section, so it is trivial there.

lead_note: 16:17 UTC (reviewer R-fls): the blueprint uses this node to split extensions of finite locally constant sheaves étale-locally; that is false for non-semisimple Lambda (Z/2 -> Z/4 -> Z/2); any split of this node must state exactly what it proves and not the splitting of extensions.
